outlook.statement: Plans for the future include diversification of product portfolio, addition of new capacities, exploring new geographies; vision anchored in lifestyle evolution and market expansion.
outlook.period: Future / next phase of growth trajectory

outlook.statement: Remain optimistic about growth of Indian Textile Industry in the long term; inherent competitive advantages continue to position it favorably for long-term growth.
The Company proposes not to transfer any amount to the reserves and an amount of Rs. 1,964.12 Lakhs (Other Equity 15,291.38 Lakhs) proposed to be retained in the Profit & Loss A/c.

To conserve the resources of the company for its activities/expansion the board, do not proposes any dividend for the F.Y. ended 31.03.2026 and carried forward the net profit balance to the next year.

The Company reported Revenue from Operation of Rs.71,070.33 lakhs as compared to Rs. 69,691.73 lakhs in the previous year which showed a Increase by 1.98%. Profit after tax of the company has been increase from Rs. 1,925.27 Lakhs to 1,964.12 lakhs Rs. which showed an increase by 2.02 %.

There have been no material changes and commitments, if any, affecting the financial position of the Company which have occurred between the end of the financial year of the Company to which the financial statements relate and the date of the report.

During the year under review there has been no such significant and material orders passed by the regulators or courts or tribunals impacting the going concern status and company's operations in future.

The Indian cotton yarn industry in 2026 faces a recovery driven by stable demand, improving export volumes, and modernizing spinning units, though tempered by regulatory and raw material cost pressures.

The future of the Indian denim market is poised for continued growth and evolution, driven by changing consumer preferences, technological advancements, and sustainability imperatives. Integration of smart technologies, wearable sensors, performance-enhancing fabrics, circular economy principles, and eco-friendly denim alternatives are expected to shape the future landscape.

India's denim industry represents a multibillion-dollar market driven by massive demographic shift and low per-capita consumption of 0.4 pairs annually. Major opportunities lie in capturing rural and Tier-II/III domestic retail booms, scaling apparel exports to replace China, and adopting eco-friendly sustainable manufacturing. Urbanization expected to support higher growth.
The current committed lines of Credit are sufficient to meet its short to medium term expansion needs.

risks: Forward-looking statements subject to risks, uncertainties, and inaccurate assumptions; actual results could vary materially
Environmental, health and safety expectations from customers increasing
Labour costs on the rise
Quality of power available from Ajmer Vidhut Vitran Nigam Limited causing frequent interruption in manufacturing process
Margin Pressures: Reduced export incentive benefits (such as cuts in RoDTEP rates) have squeezed net exporter margins.
Supply Volatility: Ongoing fluctuations in domestic raw cotton prices and international market uncertainties threaten consistent profitability.
The possibility of renewed Middle East conflict looms large and could extend commodity price volatility, further threaten supply chains, raise prices, and weigh on financial conditions.
Trade fragmentation could accelerate, possibly hurting output and increasing prices.
A possible correction in technology-driven expectations adds to the downside risks, whereas eroded policy buffers can amplify those risks.
Business Operational Risk: Inadequate/failed internal processes, people, systems, external events like economic conditions, competition, new players, natural disasters, political/military turmoil
Raw Material Risk: Volatility in prices of cotton, transportation costs

Manufacturing Risk: Machinery unavailability, breakdown, obsolescence, power supply disruption, performance below efficiency levels, labor disputes, finite machine lifespan, replacement parts availability
Quality Risk: Consumer expectations, customer preferences, fashion trends, failure to maintain product quality standards
Foreign Exchange/Currency Risk: Vulnerability to foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations affecting operating results and financial situation

Competition Risk: Intense global competition from low-cost hubs like Bangladesh and Vietnam, high competition from established brands, difficulty balancing price and quality when competitors offer cheaper prices

Raw material cost volatility: High raw material costs, global oversupply, fierce export competition, pollution-related factory shutdowns in China/Europe spiking basic raw material prices, unpredictable market conditions, weather, policies affecting raw material supply and costs
Sustainability regulations: Strict global sustainability regulations demanding expensive eco-friendly and water-efficient manufacturing upgrades
Overcapacity: Massive overcapacity leading to compressed margins
Competition from organized and unorganized companies in textile industry
Customer concentration risk - fall in revenue, rising competition, or change in demand from key clients
Global risk - lack of offshore office limits ability to capitalize on worldwide garment market opportunities
Political risk - government policy changes impacting profitability
Technological risk - need for constant upgrades in machinery, production processes, and capacity expansion to survive in competitive market

Fluctuations in finished goods prices, raw materials costs and availability, global and domestic demand supply conditions, exchange rates, government regulations and tax structure, economic developments, ability to manage growth, competition, economic growth in India, ability to attract and retain skilled professionals, time and cost overruns on contracts, government policies on investments, fiscal deficits, regulation
Interest Risk: A decrease in the bond interest rate will increase the Plan Liability.
Longevity Risk: An increase in the life expectancy of the Plan participants will increase the Plan's Liability.
Salary Risk: An increase in the salary of the plan participants will increase the Plan's Liability.
Market Risk: Foreign Currency Risk, Interest Risk, Equity Price and Commodity Prices.
Credit Risk: Counterparty default on contractual obligations.
